transcript.text: "Rahul and I never did finish talking about that question — that was 12 days back. You're not Rahul. Still on your mind?"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
"What do you think?"
"You really want my take? ...Yeah. Okay. I think we're being tested."
"How can I help?"
"The pantry's nearly bare. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"Sure."
You walk to the tree line with Elena. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"What’s going on out there?"
"Since Rahul died... I keep expecting to see Rahul at the fire. Stupid."
"About that favor — we never finished."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Meet me at the south slope below the meadow and we'll fill packs before dark."
"About what's been happening — we never finished."
"Sleep's gone strange. I sit apart to eat at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Tell me more."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Tell me more."
"I'm picking up Rahul's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Keep going."
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
"Tell me more."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

transcript.text: "About that question — What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed? Do you understand?"
"Yes. I don't want to get into what. But yes."
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
"Yeah?"
Whatever warmth was building cools to politeness.
"Yeah?"
"The math doesn't add up out here. Be kind to yourself about the remainders."
"Want to come with me?"
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"What’s going on out there?"
"Rahul is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"About that question — we never finished."
"Huh. I wouldn't have guessed that about you."
"Yeah?"
Their voice loosens. The guardedness thins.
"Yeah?"
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
"I heard them too."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
"Yeah?"
"If you hear it again — wake me. I mean that. Nobody listens alone. Not that it matters."
